analytic.title: Real Time Laser Tracking

div.p: Tracking algorithms are a vast, vibrant and com-plex area of research in computer vision and due to their increased utilization in the commercial application they have propelled re-searchers to continuously devise more efficient and competitive algorithms. Laser tracking, by definition, is to track a blob of light over a sequence of images. Most of the laser tracking algorithms in literature deal with pre-recorded videos, however, most of the scenarios in which it is used demand real-time response on a relative memory and compute constrained environment with a very low margin of error. It becomes pivotal to analyse the real-time performance of any algorithm before it is used in these cases. Hence the extensive study under this topic is taken. We develop an algorithm to satisfy this criterion (real-time) while still consuming 52 percent less memory compared to widely used algorithm background subtraction.

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: Tracking is one of the fundamental tasks in video applications that require some thought about objects of interest as it enables objects to correspond between frames. Timing is one of the most important parts of defining a realtime computer system, and performance in running the software becomes very important. A real-time system is one that is deemed as failed if it is unable to meet the deadline, which might result in catastrophic damage. There are two broad categories in this system, hard real-time and soft real-time. There is also a third category, fixed real-time systems, which lie between hard and soft real-time systems. A hard real-time system is one that has to perform without failure to meet deadlines. As soon the system fails to meet one of the performance criteria or deadlines, it fails. An example of a hard real-time system can be a flight control system, which requires a hardbound on the response time, if it fails to respond within that bound it might lead to a disastrous outcome, a classic example being the plane crash of Ethiopian Airlines in march 2019. A soft real-time system is one that on average meets the deadline required without causing any serious damage to the system. This implies that the system will not fail if a performance criterion is missed in situations that is not critical. However, if the system fails repeatedly to meet the deadlines then it cannot be characterised as a real-time system. An example would be modern streaming devices, which rely on the internet for content. The system compensates for occasional miss of deadlines with stored content in the form of buffer. The goal of the tracking algorithm is how accurately it can estimate the position of the object in the next frame based on the position and properties of the object in the first frame.

div.head: II. RELATED WORK
div.p: Laser Point Tracking is an algorithm for laser-generated blob. It essentially uses features such as color, brightness and area to track the blurred trails of fast moving laser pointer. Further research was made to detect the situation of multiple lasers in the scene. The acquired results were promising. The presented algorithm for tracking multiple laser points in the paper Ryt et al. can be applied to variety of multimedia applications e.g. camera guidance using gimbals during lectures or laser shooting ranges. Most algorithms detect all the potential objects thus requires additional time. In the paper Zhou et al proposed a model that made object as a single point and detectors used keypoint estimation to get the centre points and reduce the response time.

Fukuchi A. et al discusses camera-tracked laser pointers based interactive display. The author proposes use of bitmap image of laser trail to track over position based tracking system. However, the algorithm fails to produce meet the real time deadline as the algorithm results in delay of about 0.1 sec. Mörwald et al proposes three novel methods to increase the robustness and accuracy and also to provide basis for the further algorithms based on the tracking state detection. The algorithm extends the Monte Carlo particle filtering with confidence dependent variation along with iterative particle filtering leading to faster convergence and higher accuracy, while use of fixed particle poses removes jitter and ensures convergence.
Here the convergence refers to whether the state has already been detected.

div.head: III. METHODOLOGY
div.p: Our design methodology involves the cycle whose steps are given in figure 1. During the first phase, design of an algorithm based on our problem statement is undertaken. A chart of current algorithms and their sophistication helped us to think our way through the problem and the level of sophistication needed in-order to achieve comparable results in terms of current tracking algorithms performance and accuracy. Testing of masking algorithm both the simulation and correctness of the function implemented using software tools was made. Using profiling and experimental data the real time analysis is made. And then comparison of the masking algorithm was made with background subtraction algorithm, which is one of the widely adopted algorithm used for real time tracking using stationary camera. To choose a Fig. 1. Methodology right platform for a particular system we need to look into many factors and are often influenced by cost, development time and to obtain the real time requirements of the system. Traditionally, for the developers to have complete control on the system many of the real-time systems don't use multi-tasking or real-time operating system. With a huge development in increasing the performance of the CPUs and making it more powerful, and increase in requirement of features for every new generation of a system, this approach is becoming less common. Also, for a given hardware with highly optimized code makes the software difficult to port to a completely new platform. So for portability and reproducibility, Intel core-i5 8th gen CPU for our testing purpose is used, although the x86 architecture isn't used for embedded platforms the benchmarks of the CPU's of embedded systems are closing the gap between performance and power capability.

div.head: IV. ALGORITHM
div.p: Now looking into the detailed working of masking algorithm used in the project it is clear that the inner working of masking algorithm and background subtraction algorithm is shown. Now while going into the brief of masking algorithm and its implementation details will render the various library functions used in our algorithm and the underlying processes that runs behind those library functions for a more detailed analysis of our algorithm and further optimizations in places where more performance can be leached out of the existing function. Coming to the working of our first algorithm i.e. masking algorithm. Initially using cv2.VideoCapture() function, the real time video is captured using webcam or load up an existing video file. Later a while loop is initialized which captures frames from the captured video. This frame captured is currently in RGB format. For easier processing of the frame, the RGB frame is converted to HSV (Hue Saturation Value) format, and the later processing will be done on this HSV frame.(HSV colorsapce (hue, saturation, value) is a model that represents the colorspace similar to the RGB color model. It represents the colors in terms of saturation representing from gray to full saturated and thus it is very helpful in image processing tasks to segment objects based on color.) Using the numpy array the lower and upper HSV values of the color of the object of interest is provided. The algorithm tracks object of interest of the given color and thus the lower and upper HSV values for the color of interest are given as input for the function inRange(). This function masks all the color on the current frame within the given range. Later findContours() function is used to create a list of all contours that are masked in the previous step. If there are multiple objects having the same color as the color of object of interest, all these objects will be masked. Since just one of the counter is being tracked i.e., object of interest is assumed to be the largest contour is our object of interest. So the list is sorted that includes all the contours obtained in the previous step in terms of their areas and only select the largest among them.

Later the center of the largest counter a math formula and obtain its x and y axis values and using these values are calculated, a horizontal and a vertical line is drawn that keeps the track of the object of our interest.

HSV colorspace makes easy to segment object because in RGB colorspace it is difficult to segment image based on it color as they are coded using three channels. find_contours: One of the most important function that is used in our algorithm is the find_contours function, contours can be explained simply as a curve joining all the continuous points (along the boundary), having same color or intensity. The contours are a useful tool for shape analysis and object detection and recognition. The find_contours function does not modifies the source image but returns a modified image as the first of three return parameters. It uses Canny edge detection algorithm to find the contours and then returns a list of these contours. The process of canny edge detection can be broken down into 5 step: a. Noise is removed by applying the Gaussian filter to obtain the smooth the image. b. Intensity gradients of the image are found. c. To get rid of response to edge detection gradient magnitude thresholding suppression is applied. d. To find potential edges double threshold is applied. e. Finally the detection of edges is done by compressing all other weak edges. In the background subtraction algorithm frame of difference method is used which has the merit of strong environment adaptability. However, if the texture of back-ground matches with the tracking object, the information of movement may get lost. Although background subtraction algorithm can extract information of moving object, it fails to meet the accuracy and real time constraints, as it generalizes over the whole scene rather than on a single object of interest. The initial moving region is determined by the frame difference method. This initial moving region is then subjected to background subtraction to get a more accurate moving region. The tracking features of the object are extracted in the determined moving region. Further mean-shift method is used to track the moving object.

div.head: Fig. 2. Background Subtraction Algorithm
div.p: The object contour is obtained by the two frames in video image sequences and this is the frame difference. The moving object in the image sequence or video can be detected if the absolute value of the difference of their brightness by the two frames subtraction is larger than the certain threshold. Using this brightness difference the moving object in the image sequence or video can be tracked. The advantage of the frame difference is that its robust nature to detect even the slightest of the luminescence changes. But the major drawback of the background subtraction algorithm is that it can only extract the boundary of the object which is constantly in motion and its performance is highly reliable on the interval of inter frames chosen by the user. A smaller time interval is chosen when the objects in the video or image sequence are constantly and rapidly moving. The objects will not overlap in the two frames if the time interval is not chosen accurately.

A larger time interval is needed if the objects are moving slowly. If time interval chosen for objects moving slowly is too small, the object will not be detected as the object will be almost completely overlapped between two alternative frames.

div.head: VI. RESULTS
div.p: For both the algorithms described previously we perform a set of experiments with detailed analysis using the above formulation to calculate the response time. Throughout this section, we show the comparison between masking and background subtraction algorithm with respect to response time and memory usage. We then also perform response time analysis based on the video quality of the pre-recorded video. Figure 3 show the real time object being tracked. A vertical and a horizontal lines are used to track the exact location of the object of interest. The point of intersection of these two lines indicate the center of the object of interest which in this case is a red laser point.

div.head: A. Memory Performance
div.p: In Table I we see maximum dynamic memory utilization of the both the algorithms. It is also worth noticing that the maximum dynamic memory utilization of these algorithms comes at different times for the same inputs. It is clear that masking algorithm uses about 50% less memory with respect to the background subtraction algorithm, which is one of the most important criteria in the real of embedded systems due to limited memory in the same.

div.head: B. Timing Performance
div.p: Now comparing the total time taken to render a prerecorded 720p video of length 24 seconds at 60fps, we see that there is about 10 seconds of additional time required for the background subtraction algorithm to process the frames, which results in drop of frames per second from 60 to 47, while the masking algorithm is able to process the frames at a speed greater than the frames of the original video resulting an increase in fps from 60 to 68. From the code profiling we see that number of lines of code in the background subtraction algorithm which exceeds 4ms are twice than that of the masking algorithm, thus increasing the computational requirement for the process to increase, which in-turn increases the pre-emption of the process from higher levels acting as bottleneck for the performance of the algorithm to process frames at higher rate.

div.p: The masking algorithm utilizes inRange() function. This function masks all the pixels falling in the HSV colorspace of object of interest which is provided my the user in terms of numpy array.

div.head: VII. CONCLUSION
div.p: In this paper we propose a new algorithm for tracking lasers in real time, followed by an comparison with one of the widely used algorithm in this domain, i.e., background subtraction algorithm. The necessary conditions and theoretical analysis of response time calculation was done followed by practical experiments, showing an improvement in both memory as well as timing performance of our algorithm.

Analysis of time taken by the specific functions and the number of hits of each line in the code by using time profiling and memory profiling on both the algorithms roots up to a conclusion that masking algorithm consumes 52% less memory compared to background subtraction algorithm and 57% less response time as compared to background subtraction algorithm. While the algorithm was extensively checked to eliminate any uncertainty in the execution part and to guarantee the hard limit of response time, which is a necessary condition for system to be real time.
Some of the brief inferences from the experiments are also summarised below,

• As the video resolution increases, the response time of the algorithm also increases. So better tracking performance can be achieved by scaling down the resolution of the input video. • There is an exponential growth in the response time for the algorithm when the video resolution increases from 720p to 1080p. If the input video quality above 720p, the response time of the algorithm can be effectively decreased by scaling down the resolution.

div.head: VIII. FUTURE SCOPE
div.p: • Generalize to a wider range of object tracking by adding additional features to the current algorithms.
• Compression of the frames to reduce the memory foot-print. • Better color accuracy even in low lighting.
• Memory based tracking of a particular object.
• Use of Kalman filter for occluded objects
